title: Introduce credential-metrics bridge and typed stream handles for tri-SDKs
author: Priya Nair
ci_status: pass after one flaky test rerun
release_notes: Adds a credential telemetry bridge and typed streaming handles across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; improves retry telemetry, reduces stream memory copies, and bumps SDK patch versions.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight credential-metrics bridge and language-native typed stream handles for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The bridge surfaces token lifecycle events (refresh, failure, fallback) and retry/backoff transitions as low-overhead telemetry counters/tags. The typed stream handles provide a small ergonomic API that wraps the underlying streaming protocol with explicit lifecycle hooks (on_start, on_resume, on_error, on_close) and safe typed envelopes to reduce buffer copies and improve cross-language parity.

Motivation: Teams have asked for better observability into credential churn and retry behavior without having to instrument service code. Streaming ergonomics between SDKs have drifted: the TS/Go shapes exposed a few helpers that Python lacked, and Python had a more heavyweight iterator model that caused extra buffering. This change aims to: 1) provide consistent telemetry (counts + last-event tags) for credential operations across SDKs, 2) unify streaming ergonomics (typed handles and lifecycle hooks), and 3) make a small performance win by avoiding an extra frame copy on chunk assembly.

High-level changes: - Add credential_metrics module that emits: credential.refresh.count, credential.refresh.duration_ms.p95, credential.refresh.failures, credential.refresh.fallbacks, stream.resume.count. Metrics are emitted via existing telemetry hooks (no new exporter required). - Introduce typed stream handles in each SDK with the same public surface: start(options), next(), resume(), close(), and lifecycle callbacks. Implementations translate to native async iterables / async generators / channels idiomatically per language. - Hook credential events into the SDK retry machinery so retry/backoff transitions increment a metric and attach a last-event tag for quick query. - Minimal public API additions: a new optional SDK config key: credential_telemetry: { enabled: boolean, namespace: string } (default off). - Add examples and docs and bump SDK patch versions.

Files touched (high level): see changed_files. Tests: added unit tests for credential event emission in each SDK and integration smoke tests for typed stream handles across a local test harness. CI: one flaky TypeScript test (stream-heartbeat.spec) failed on the first run due to timing; was retried and passed. All other suites green.

Commits summary: - c8f3a1d: Add credential metrics bridge (py/ts/go) and wire into retry paths. - b4ef9a2: Implement typed stream handle for Python and TS; add examples. - 9d2b7c1: Go typed handle + perf tweak to chunk assembly; tests and docs.

Review conversation (abridged): - Lena Ortiz: "Can we keep the default disabled for telemetry and document the cost/volume tradeoff?" -> Author: "Yes — credential_telemetry defaults to false; updated docs and examples to show enabling and query examples." - Graham McKee: "The typed handle API looks good, but can we reduce allocations in the Python iterator when resuming?" -> Author: "Addressed in second commit: use memoryview-backed buffer slices and preallocate a small chunk pool; added test asserting zero extra copy on resume path." - Sophie Laurent: "Please add a note to the changelog about the TS test flakiness and the retry on CI." -> Author: "Done; CI note added and flaky test marked with ephemeral tag while we evaluate upstream timing variance"

Performance notes: Microbenchmarks show ~8-12% lower median memory allocation per stream in Python when using the typed handle vs old iterator for 2KB chunk workloads. TS and Go saw negligible CPU change, and Go saw ~6% lower heap churn due to avoiding an intermediate buffer during chunk concat.

Backward compatibility: All changes are additive. credential_telemetry is opt-in. Typed stream handles are provided alongside existing streaming helpers and can be adopted incrementally. No breaking changes to existing calls.

Release plan: - Bump Python SDK to 2.6.0, TS SDK to 1.12.0, Go SDK to 1.5.3. - Publish docs/metrics.md with examples and recommended Grafana/PromQL snippets. - Announce in SDK changelog and suggest opt-in rollout.

Merge: Squashed and merged after approvals; merge commit includes a short migration note and links to the Linear tasks.
notes_for_followup: Monitor credential.refresh.* cardinality in staging when teams opt-in
Observe TS stream-heartbeat flakiness root cause (timing window) and consider increasing CI harness timeouts
Consider an opt-out sampling mode if telemetry shows high cardinality across many service tokens
